newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money holds despite tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money holds despite tax payments.

text.p: * Volume falls to 16.847 bln from 17.974 bln pesos
Manila overnight money was unchanged on Tuesday at an average of 10.03125 percent despite the remittance of billions of pesos of tax payments, dealers said.
They estimated banks transferred on Monday 18 to 25 billion pesos worth of income tax payments to the government.
"It's still very liquid," a foreign bank dealer said, saying the outflow was partly offset by the maturities of 10 billion pesos worth of floating rate treasury notes.
"Some banks are not feeling at all the impact of the tax remittance," he added.
Rates were wedged in the same range of 10.25 to 10.03125 percent, with 33 lenders and 20 borrowers.
In the secondary market, banks were initially tentative on buying bills as they weighed the liquidity effect of the tax remittance in the overnight market, dealers said.
After coming to the conclusion that the market remained liquid, banks began buying T-bills.
"The one year-bills were preferred because banks find the rates toppish (reaching top) at these levels," a dealer said.
A Reuters poll of six financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.30 to 10.50 percent for the three-month bills; 10.70 to 10.90 percent for the six months; and 11.20 to 11.50 for the one-year bills.
